label: VERIFIED SNAPSHOT — real NASA open data from 4 missions

sources.title: Mars MGS MOLA Digital Elevation Model, global mosaic
sources.archive_node: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Cartography and Imaging Science Node
processing_chain: Windowed /vsicurl read of 128.0x115.2 px from 46080x23040 global mosaic
caveats: Native 463 m/px versus the 177.5 m x 187.1 m grid cell; relief below the source resolution is not resolved.

sources.title: Slope and traversability derived from MOLA elevation
sources.archive_node: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Cartography and Imaging Science Node
processing_chain: slope = degrees(arctan(|grad(elevation)|)) with 177.5 m NS / 187.1 m EW spacing
traversability = banded cost multiplier per docs/nasa-data-catalog.md (0-5deg=1.0, 5-10=1.5, 10-15=2.5, 15-20=5.0, 20-25=10.0, >25=impassable)
caveats: Slope inherits MOLA's 463 m/px resolution: real obstacles smaller than ~463 m are not represented.

sources.title: THEMIS Night Infrared controlled mosaic, global, v2 (Oct 2018)
sources.archive_node: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Cartography and Imaging Science Node
processing_chain: Normalised to 0-1 across the 2nd-98th percentile of the window
caveats: This is night-IR brightness normalised as a thermal inertia PROXY, not a published thermal inertia product. High values indicate heat-retaining (likely rocky) surfaces; low values indicate fast-cooling dust or loose sand.

sources.title: Jezero Crater CTX block-adjusted mosaic (Exploration Zone)
sources.archive_node: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Cartography and Imaging Science Node
processing_chain: Windowed /vsicurl read of 11854.9x10669.4 px from 44076x41960 regional mosaic
Bilinear decimation to 300x300 for the basemap raster
caveats: Decimated from ~5 m/px to the computation grid for display. The full-resolution mosaic is used for map tiles, not for routing.

sources.title: Composite traverse hazard derived from MOLA slope and THEMIS night IR
sources.archive_node: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Cartography and Imaging Science Node
caveats: Hazard is a VICTOR weighting of measured inputs, not a NASA hazard product. The weights are a modelling choice.

sources.title: CRISM MRDR multispectral summary parameters, tile 20N078 (MC-13)
sources.instrument: CRISM (Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars)
sources.distributor: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Washington University in St. Louis)
sources.archive_node: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Geosciences Node
sources.native_crs: Equirectangular, per-tile sphere; read via published 5x5 deg bounds
processing_chain: HTTP range read of 1.8 MB from the 576 MB ENVI BSQ cube (band 16 OLINDEX3, band 53 CINDEX2)
Georeferenced via the product label's published 5x5 degree bounds
caveats: CRISM multispectral mapping has swath gaps: only 66% of the window is measured. Unmeasured cells are stored as -9999 and must be treated as NO DATA, never as 'no mineral'.
Summary parameters are spectral indices, not mineral abundances.

sources.title: Science priority from CRISM mineralogy and published Jezero targets
sources.instrument: CRISM summary parameters + Perseverance science targeting
sources.archive_node: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Geosciences Node
processing_chain: 10 published science targets with literature coordinates
mineral = normalised max(OLINDEX3, CINDEX2) from real CRISM spectra
science = 0.6*mineral + 0.4*target_model where CRISM measured; target_model alone inside CRISM swath gaps
caveats: A priority SCORE, not a measurement. The mineral indices underneath it are real CRISM measurements; collapsing them into one priority number is a VICTOR modelling choice.
66% of cells are CRISM-measured (DERIVED); the rest fall back to the target proximity model (MODELLED). Per-cell provenance therefore varies across the grid.
Target sources: Ehlmann et al. 2008; Farley et al. 2022 (Science 377); Goudge et al. 2015; Goudge et al. 2017; Goudge et al. 2017; Farley et al. 2020; Mangold et al. 2021
